title: Flowers for Algernon
note: Told through Charlie Gordon's progress reports — his rise and heartbreaking fall in intelligence is a modern tragedy that stays with you long after the last page. A masterpiece of science fiction.
author: Daniel Keyes

title: The Old Man and the Sea
note: Hemingway's spare, beautiful tale of Santiago — an aging fisherman's lonely struggle against the marlin and the sea. A quiet meditation on endurance, pride, and the dignity of never giving up.
author: Ernest Hemingway

title: Kaze no Matasaburō (Matasaburō of the Wind)
note: A gentle, dreamlike children's tale by Kenji Miyazawa about a boy the village children suspect is the wind spirit himself. Whimsical and quietly magical — a beloved piece of Japanese literature.
author: Kenji Miyazawa

title: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
note: Oscar Wilde's beloved collection of five fairy tales — The Happy Prince, The Nightingale and the Rose, The Selfish Giant, The Devoted Friend, and The Remarkable Rocket. Tender, witty, and quietly melancholic, each carries a moral wrapped in luminous prose.
author: Oscar Wilde
